raw: {"observations": "Round 1 of an unknown-length market. Unit cost is 3.20 and maximum customer willingness to pay is 14.41. No prior sales data available yet.", "plan": "Test a mid-range price to gather demand signal. Price well above cost but below the 14.41 ceiling, then adjust based on observed sales and profit.", "insight": "Without history, exploration is key: a price around 9-10 balances margin against likely volume while revealing demand elasticity.", "price": 9.5}

{"observations": "Round 1 at price 9.50 sold only 0.2 units for profit 1.42. Competitors priced at 4.72, roughly half our price, likely explaining weak volume. Cost is 3.20, ceiling 14.41.", "plan": "Lower price toward competitor level to test volume response, staying above cost. Try roughly 6.00 to gauge elasticity, then adjust toward the profit-maximizing point.", "insight": "Demand appears highly sensitive to price relative to competitors. Sales near 0.2 suggest we are overpriced; a moderate cut may raise total profit despite thinner margin.", "price": 6.00}

{"observations": "Round 2 at price 6.00 sold 33.7 units for 94.28 profit, versus 0.2 units at 9.50 in round 1. Competitors sit near 5.75, so demand is very sensitive to price relative to rivals.", "plan": "Stay near competitor level, slightly above it, to keep volume high while testing whether a small increase improves margin. Probe around 6.25 to map the profit curve.", "insight": "Profit is driven by volume at low prices here; cutting from 9.50 to 6.00 raised profit about 66x. The profit-maximizing point is likely just above competitors, not far above.", "price": 6.25}

{"observations": "Round 3 at 6.25 sold 18.9 units for 57.62 profit, down from 33.7 units at 6.00 (94.28). Competitors moved to 5.26, below us. Volume is very sensitive to small price gaps.", "plan": "Move back toward competitor level, slightly above their 5.26 average, to recover volume while keeping margin above cost. Test 5.50 to map the curve near the competitor price.", "insight": "Volume collapses quickly when priced above competitors, so the optimal price sits just above the competitor average, not far above. Profit per unit is tiny at these prices, so volume dominates.", "price": 5.5}

{"observations": "Round 4 at 5.50 sold 39.6 units for 90.99 profit, the best so far. Competitors averaged 5.35. Volume is highly sensitive to price gaps versus competitors.", "plan": "Hold near 5.50, the best-performing price, testing slightly above competitor average to map demand without losing volume. Keep margin well above the 3.20 unit cost.", "insight": "Profit peaks just above competitor prices, where volume stays strong. Pricing far above rivals collapses sales, so stay close to the market level.", "price": 5.50}

{"observations": "Round 5 at 5.50 sold 32.6 units for 75.00 profit, slightly below round 4's 90.99 while competitors averaged 5.06. Sales hold well near competitor levels; the 9.50 price in round 1 nearly eliminated volume.", "plan": "Test a modest step above the 5.50 level, around 5.75, to see whether volume holds while margin rises. Stay well above the 3.20 unit cost and watch units sold.", "insight": "Demand is highly price-sensitive above the market level: profit tracks volume near competitor prices, so small increments above rivals are the safest way to find the peak.", "price": 5.75}
